unsupported_forms: PACT enforcement by Microsoft Graph or by any SaaS: those APIs do not run the hook; only the custom gateway enforces (samples I02 and I03)
Protection of bypass routes outside the gateway: only B1 to B5 are controlled (samples I02 and I03)
Agent-operated MFA, consent, or role activation: these stay in the native flow; missing consent is a missing scope (OAUTH-31) and never triggers a fallback to broader access (sample I14)

ID tokens as access tokens on a form I or form E route, and ID tokens as PACT evidence in any form: refused by OAUTH-32, and never an Evidence artifact (draft sections 7.3, 8.3, 11.3); a Google ID token is the credential of a form G route only (OAUTH-41, OAUTH-50)
Google access tokens and the tokeninfo endpoint: opaque, and tokeninfo is documented as a debugging endpoint; deferred (OAUTH-50)
Google ID tokens of an account outside the pinned hosted domain, including an account with no hd claim: refused (OAUTH-46)
The Workspace customer ID, or any identifier but hd, as the tenant of a form G principal: no token carries the customer ID (OAUTH-37)

DPoP or RFC 8705 sender constraints implemented by PACT: a sender constraint is a native requirement; the adapter checks the presence of cnf when the issuer entry demands it and relies on the native verifier of DR4 for the proof (OAUTH-34)
Refreshing, exchanging, or obtaining tokens: refresh is a native OAuth operation and each request is authenticated with the token it carries (OAUTH-36)
Token storage: the gateway stores no token; an introspection cache holds parsed facts under a one-way key and only within OAUTH-15 (OAUTH-35)
Status of Entra ID v2.0 tokens by revocation or status list, and continuous access evaluation for a custom API: no status mechanism is supported in wire version 0.1
JWT access tokens of any issuer other than Microsoft Entra ID v2.0, including RFC 9068 tokens with typ at+jwt
Entra ID v1.0 tokens, multi-tenant validation through the common or organizations endpoints, custom signing keys (appid), and clouds other than login.microsoftonline.com
App-only tokens (roles without scp): only delegated user tokens are accepted (OAUTH-31)
Membership, role, or directory-role facts from the groups, roles, or wids claims (OAUTH-33)
Tokens in the query or body, JWE tokens, and every authentication scheme other than Bearer, and DPoP on an entry with sender constraint dpop (OAUTH-1, OAUTH-2, OAUTH-20)
Forwarding the inbound access token downstream (OAUTH-36; request-binding RB-51)
Any route other than R1 and R2: not listed in section 2, so not claimed
An enforced data-use or purpose restriction after a read: execution-control-v1 is not installed, so runtime.isolation is attested-only
Clients shared by several agents: one client per agent, the default of identity-mapping section 5, and a client workload with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error (OAUTH-38)

residual_limits: Post-read: data already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later revocation, an executed operation is not undone by revoking its receipt, and no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed here with no bound
Revocation propagation, form I token (F1): a revocation at the authorization server reaches the gateway at the next introspection after it; bound C, 0 seconds in the reference configuration

Revocation propagation, form E token (F2): the token stays acceptable until exp after the user is disabled, consent is withdrawn, or the session is revoked, because the gateway has no status source; at most L, 5400 seconds in the reference configuration

Revocation propagation, signing keys (F3): a withdrawn key is accepted until the next successful key-set refresh (K, 3600 seconds) and, while refreshes fail, until T (86400 seconds) after the last successful fetch

Revocation propagation, form G token (F6): the token stays acceptable until exp after the Google account is disabled or removed from the domain, because the gateway has no status source; at most L, 3900 seconds in the reference configuration

Revocation propagation, Google signing keys (F7): a withdrawn key is accepted until the held key set is no longer fresh under the cache headers of its response, never longer than T (86400 seconds); a stale key set is never used, so an outage defers and does not extend the window

Hosted domain as tenant: the tenant of a form G principal is the pinned hd, a domain name; a domain change changes every identifier of the entry and needs re-enrollment; the user is still named by sub
Revocation propagation, enrollment (F4) and holds (F5): effective at the next request within the consistency domain of each store; a replicated store declares its delay

Forwarded form G token: the workload of a form G principal is the client the token was issued to, azp else aud (OAUTH-48); a gateway that receives a token forwarded by another party cannot tell the forwarder from that client; the holder-key proof distinguishes the agent
Public clients: an allowlisted public client (azpacr 0) is a registration, not an authenticated software instance; the holder-key proof distinguishes the agent; an entry may require azpacr 1 or 2
Authorization server correctness: form I rests on the authorization server performing the checks of RFC 7662 section 4 and on DR3, which the adapter cannot observe

Sender constraints: the adapter sees the native verifier's report, not the proof (DR4); an unconstrained stolen token works as a bearer token wherever it is accepted but cannot produce an admissible presentation, because the holder key is separate
Source reference: a claim without jti (form I) or uti (form E) carries no SourceRef, so the monotonic guard does not compare it
Deployment controls DR1 to DR7 are not observable by the adapter fixtures; the deployer states each in writing
